title: Properness tested on DVRs of the generic function field
statement: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $f:R\to S$ be separated and of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with $R$ integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], generic point $\xi$ [def-sc-generic-point], and function field $L=\kappa(\xi)$ [def-sc-function-field]. Suppose that for every discrete valuation subring $A\subset L$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with fraction field $L$, and every morphism $b:\operatorname{Spec}A\to S$ whose generic restriction is $\operatorname{Spec}L\to R\xrightarrow{f}S$, the canonical generic-point morphism $\operatorname{Spec}L\to R$ extends to a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}A\to R$ over $b$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then $f$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Conversely properness implies this extension property. The extension, whenever it exists, is unique.

source.place: Tag 0208, limits-lemma-Noetherian-dvr-valuative-proper, equivalence (1) and (4), specialized to an integral source; separatedness supplies uniqueness.

proof.text: Cover $S$ by Noetherian affine opens $V$. Each nonempty inverse image $R_V$ is integral with generic field $L$; the restrictions remain separated and finite type by base change. A test over $V$ extends into $R$ by hypothesis and factors through $R_V$, since its composite to $S$ factors through $V$. Empty inverse images are universally closed. Universal closedness is local here: for $T\to S$ and closed $D\subset R_T$, its image intersects $T_V$ in the image of the closed inverse image of $D$ in $(R_V)_{T_V}$. Closedness on this open cover implies closedness in $T$. Hence fix $V$ and rename it $S$.

Apply the integral Chow-envelope compactification lemma: obtain $\pi:Y\to R$, $j:Y\to P$, $Y\subset Z\subset P$ and $U$, with $\pi$ proper surjective, $Z$ integral Noetherian proper over $S$, and all generic maps identified over $L$.

If $j(Y)$ is not closed, take $z\in Z\setminus Y$. The generic point lies in $Y$, so $z$ is nongeneric. The same-field trait lemma gives $a_Z:\operatorname{Spec}A\to Z$ with closed image $z$ and canonical generic restriction over $L$; put $a=c\circ a_Z$.

Put $b=(P\to S)\circ a$. The generic restriction of $b$ is the composite $\operatorname{Spec}L\to R\to S$, because $Y\to R$ is the identity over the dense open $U$. The hypothesis therefore gives $r:\operatorname{Spec}A\to R$ over $b$ extending the canonical generic point. Apply valuative existence to the proper map $\pi:Y\to R$ and the square whose generic map is the canonical $\operatorname{Spec}L\to Y$ and whose bottom is $r$. A DVR is a valuation ring by its defining equivalence. We obtain $h:\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$ extending that generic map. The two $S$-maps $j\circ h$ and $a$ into $P$ have equal generic restrictions. Projective space is proper, hence separated, and valuative uniqueness makes them equal. Their closed-point values cannot agree: the first is in $j(Y)$, the second is $z\notin j(Y)$. This contradiction proves $j(Y)$ closed.
An immersion with closed image is a closed immersion, so $j:Y\to P$ is a closed immersion. Combining properness of closed immersions, properness of $P\to S$, and composition, $Y\to S$ is proper.

For $T\to S$ and closed $D\subseteq R_T$, put $E=\pi_T^{-1}(D)\subseteq Y_T$, which is closed. Base-changed surjectivity gives equal images of $E$ and $D$ in $T$. Properness of $Y_T\to T$ makes this image closed. Thus $R\to S$ is universally closed on each affine $V$. Step 1 then gives universal closedness over the original $S$. Original separatedness and finite type imply properness by definition.

Conversely, properness supplies every required extension by valuative existence, since a DVR is a valuation ring with fraction field $L$. Separatedness was assumed from the start, so valuative uniqueness identifies any two extensions, independently of properness. This proves the converse and uniqueness.
